description:
O Uirapuru Estelar dá voz ao que a exploração espacial deixou para trás. Na Lua e em Marte, equipamentos e sondas da NASA seguem em silêncio, mas cada um carrega uma história de projeto, descoberta e despedida. 
The Stellar Uirapuru gives a voice to what space exploration has left behind. On the Moon and Mars, NASA equipment and probes remain silent, yet each carries a story of design, discovery, and farewell.
summary: Uirapuru Estelar is an educational website that gives voice to what space exploration left behind. On the Moon and Mars, NASA’s equipment, such as lunar modules, rovers, landers, and probes, remains silent, yet each piece carries a story of design, discovery, and farewell. The site is organized into Home, Moon,  Mars and Quizz pages. Each page presents discarded equipment with its history, how it operated, how it ended, and its scientific legacy, from the Apollo modules and Surveyor landers to the Viking, Spirit, Opportunity, and Ingenuity missions, as well as probes like Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, and Kepler. The project addresses the challenge by turning “space junk” into storytelling, showing that these objects are archaeological sites and time capsules, not just waste. It is important because the public usually remembers only launches and arrivals, while what remains afterward holds knowledge that paved the way for future missions. By telling these stories in an accessible, engaging way, the project encourages curiosity, scientific memory, and respect for the legacy of space exploration.
details:
Project Overview & Functionality:

Uirapuru Estelar is a web-based storytelling platform dedicated to documenting the history and legacy of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. The website functions as a digital repository where users can navigate through specific sections (Moon, Mars, and a Quiz) to explore the narratives of objects such as the Apollo Lunar Modules, the Sojourner Rover, and the Viking Landers. For each piece of equipment, we present a structured narrative detailing its original purpose, its operational history, how the mission concluded, and the scientific legacy it left behind.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

The primary benefit of the project is reframing the concept of "space junk" as valuable archaeological sites and historical time capsules. The intended impact is to promote scientific memory and public education. While the general public is usually familiar with the launches and arrivals of space missions, our project highlights that the equipment left behind holds crucial knowledge that enabled future explorations. By presenting this information in an accessible and engaging manner, we aim to foster a deeper respect for the history of space exploration.

Tools and Technologies Used:

The platform was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. As our team is primarily composed of researchers and students, we utilized Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a practical tool to assist with specific technical demands. We applied AI to help structure and refine the CSS code, ensuring a clean and polished visual presentation for the website, and also to assist with the translation of certain content pieces. This allowed us to focus on the research and storytelling aspects of the project.

Creativity & Team Considerations:

The project's creativity lies in its conceptual approach: we used the "Uirapuru" (a bird from Brazilian folklore) as a metaphor to represent the silent voices of these abandoned machines. Furthermore, we designed the platform to be interactive, incorporating a quiz to engage the audience. When developing the project, our team carefully considered factors such as user accessibility, the educational tone of the content, the historical accuracy of the missions, and how to present complex aerospace engineering in a digestible format for the general public.
